correctness.rationale: Surface-area parametrization gives E[UUᵀ h(U)]/E h(U). Gaussian linearization plus the beta angular identity yields covariance A(I+Q)A/(d+1), Q positive definite of trace one. Strict convexity of log E||diag(e^t)G|| and permutation symmetry force q_i to reverse-order the squared semiaxes, so reverse Chebyshev proves the sharp upper scalar ratio and ball-only equality; Q positive definite gives strict lower Loewner and scalar inequalities. Explicit Gaussian bounds for collapsing one axis give the dimension-sharp infimum. Standalone verifier replayed both integral representations with finite checks; no finite computation is asserted to establish the infinite case.

value.rationale: The new result identifies exactly how surface-uniform squared pair distances compare to interior-uniform ones for every ellipsoid in every dimension, despite failure of general high-dimensional convex-body comparisons. It establishes optimal dimension-dependent constants with equality and degenerating-sharpness classification and a nontrivial covariance-matrix inequality. Gaussian angular mixture and strict majorization are structural mechanisms with potential applications to nonuniform boundary sampling and geometric statistics; it is not an arbitrary isolated numerical evaluation.
